items.title: [Bug]: speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism produces wrong output with --no-async-scheduling
items.body: With `--no-async-scheduling`, speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism produces wrong output — or a CUDA fault — instead of being rejected or working. Turning async scheduling back on fixes it. ### Root cause `next_decode_eligible_step` is assigned in exactly one place in the tree: ``` vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:49 request.next_decode_eligible_step = self.current_step + self.pp_size ``` initialised in one place: ``` vllm/v1/request.py:167 self.next_decode_eligible_step = 0 ``` and read in exactly one place: ``` vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:509 if self.current_step =0 && ind 1` + `--no-async-scheduling` at config time, with a message naming the cadence. 3. At minimum, document that speculative decoding under PP requires async scheduling. prs.title: [Bugfix][Core] Align hybrid block sizes across PP stages
prs.body: ## Purpose Fixes #51752. A pipeline stage containing only SSM/KDA layers has no local attention backend, so it skips hybrid block-size alignment. Its KV cache sizes can then disagree with attention-owning stages before frontend synchronization. Keep the existing local backend discovery and block-size computation unchanged. After local alignment, gather only four cache configuration values over the PP CPU group and use the first attention-owning stage's values on every rank. Stages without an attention backend participate with `None`; if no stage has one, configuration remains unchanged. Uninitialized and single-rank execution bypass communication. This uses one shared synchronization helper.

items.body: ### 🐛 Describe the bug Embedding quality/discrimination for `Qwen3-Embedding-8B` degrades significantly under real, sustained concurrent multi-tenant traffic (many distinct external clients hitting `/v1/embeddings` continuously), compared to the exact same model+flags served in isolation with only a single test client. **Isolated (single client, no concurrent traffic), fresh pod:** - Riddle-style discrimination test (short German lexicon entries + adversarial queries): 2/3 correct top-1 retrieval - Paraphrase vs. unrelated-sentence probe: paraphrase pairs ~0.83 cosine, unrelated pairs ~0.52 cosine — clear separation **Same model, same flags, same image, pod under real concurrent production traffic (confirmed via router logs: multiple distinct client IPs issuing `/v1/embeddings` requests every few hundred ms):** - Same riddle test: 1/3 correct top-1 - Same probe: paraphrase pairs ~0.72, unrelated pairs ~0.60 — much weaker separation, scores compressed into a narrow band regardless of semantic relationship This reproduces identically whether the client hits the vLLM pod directly (bypassing any reverse proxy) or through a router/proxy layer in front of it, ruling out the proxy as the cause. It also reproduces immediately on a **freshly restarted** pod (seconds after becoming ready, before any prefix-cache or state could plausibly accumulate) ruling out cache buildup over pod uptime as the cause. We also caught (once, not reliably reproduced) a case where a 2-item batch embedding request for two semantically unrelated sentences returned two embeddings with cosine similarity of exactly 1.0000 (vectors nearly parallel, not bit-identical) inconsistent with the same request pair's steady-state deterministic result (~0.64) measured dozens of times afterward in isolation. We could not reproduce this specific anomaly with synthetic same-process concurrent load (48 threads, single client process), only ever observed it against the real production traffic path. We ruled out the following as explanations by direct A/B testing on identical hardware/model: - **dtype (bfloat16 vs float32)**: identical results. Cross-config drift check on identical inputs: mean cosine similarity between bf16 and float32 embeddings = 0.9999, Pearson correlation of full pairwise-similarity matrices = 1.0000. - **`--pooler-config` auto-detect vs. explicit override**: vLLM already auto-resolves to `seq_pooling_type='LAST', use_activation=True` for this model with no flags set explicitly setting

items.body: `QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` supports static per-tensor activation scales together with per-output-channel weight scales. However, the legacy Triton MoE path uses the activation quantization flag to select both activation-scale and weight-scale indexing. For this combination, `per_act_token_quant=False`, so the kernel takes the tensor-scale branch even though the weights have per-channel scales. It consequently reads the weight scales using the wrong layout. This affects the existing static INT8 path independently of its planned migration to the MoE oracle. ### Expected behavior Activation and weight scales should be indexed independently: - A1/A2: use the loaded static scalar activation scales. - W13/W2: use the scale belonging to the routed expert and output channel. Changing relevant weight scales should affect the corresponding computation, while changing scales belonging only to unrouted experts should not affect the output. ### Observed behavior and reproduction outline A component probe used: - 4 experts - Hidden size and intermediate size of 128 - 8 tokens, top-k=2 - BF16 inputs - Static activation scales and nonuniform per-channel weight scales - No bias, with router weights applied on the output side The probe exercised Quark weight creation and post-load processing, then its existing `apply()` path. With fixed weights, inputs, and routing, multiplying all W13 channel scales of expert 3 by 4 produced no output change, although that expert was selected by four routing slots. An experimental patch separating weight-scale layout from activation quantization made this perturbation affect the output. The corrected legacy and manually constructed modular paths also produced identical BF16 outputs for the covered case. These are component-level observations, not a completed model evaluation or full regression result. items.body: After a failed NIXL/HMA receive, DeepSeek-V4 can return HTTP 200 with corrupted tokens in `reasoning` and an empty `content` field. Clients that read only `choices[].message.content` see an apparently empty response. Disabling thinking exposes the corrupted output in `content` instead. #### Reproduction Use disaggregated serving with DSpark disabled on Prefill and enabled on Decode. Prefill arguments: ```sh --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' ``` Decode arguments: ```sh --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --speculative-config \ '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}' \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' ``` Send chat-completion requests with `max_tokens=128` using: 1. the default request; 2. thinking explicitly enabled; 3. thinking explicitly disabled; and 4. reasoning parsing disabled. On [`793ca6998`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/793ca6998), the asymmetric configuration fails the NIXL compatibility handshake. No KV transfer completes successfully, but the requests resume decoding. #### Expected behavior With `kv_load_failure_policy="fail"`, a failed NIXL compatibility handshake or KV receive should terminate the request with an error. The API must not return HTTP 200 or expose generated tokens in either `content` or `reasoning`. #### Actual behavior A four-mode matrix ran eight requests per mode: | Request mode | HTTP 200 with 128 tokens | `content` | `reasoning` | |---|---:|---|---| | default | 8/8 | empty | corrupted output | | thinking enabled | 8/8 | empty | corrupted output | | thinking disabled | 8/8 | corrupted output | empty | | reasoning parsing disabled | 8/8 | corrupted output | empty | All 32 requests generated 128 tokens. The apparent empty output in the first two modes is therefore response-field routing, not an absence of generation. #### Cause The failed HMA receive is reported as receive completion without a request-level failure reaching the scheduler, so Decode resumes with missing KV data and generates corrupted tokens. items.title: [Bug]: ROCm MI300X FP8 KV cache MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 accuracy issues
items.body: ### Summary On ROCm/MI300X, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` starts successfully with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, and requests return HTTP 200, but generated output is severely corrupted. vLLM also reports that calibrated FP8 attention scales are unavailable and uses `1.0`: ```text Using uncalibrated q_scale 1.0 and/or prob_scale 1.0 with fp8 attention. This may cause accuracy issues. Please make sure q/prob scaling factors are available in the fp8 checkpoint. ``` That warning was initially suspected, but it is not the cause of this failure. The failure is a dtype mismatch in the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention path. This is not a small accuracy regression. GSM8K strict accuracy drops from `0.9666` with the default BF16 KV cache to `0.0099` with FP8 KV cache. Outputs contain unrelated problem fragments, incorrect arithmetic, and repetition that often continues to the generation limit. Removing only `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` restores normal output and accuracy. This appears related to #45533, but the failure mode is different: #45533 reports startup failure, while this configuration starts and serves normally but silently returns incorrect output. ### Root cause On ROCm gfx942, `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` is `torch.float8_e4m3fnuz`. The MiniMax-M3 sparse backend instead hardcodes `torch.float8_e4m3fn` when it reinterprets the byte-backed KV cache: ```python self.kv_cache_fp8_dtype = ( torch.float8_e5m2 if "e5m2" in kv_cache_dtype else torch.float8_e4m3fn ) ``` The prefill and decode wrappers also classify only `float8_e4m3fn` and `float8_e5m2` as FP8, omitting `float8_e4m3fnuz`. FN and FNUZ do not have the same encoding. Interpreting gfx942 FNUZ KV-cache bytes as FN changes the represented values before sparse attention consumes them. A direct MI300X kernel comparison measured: | KV interpretation | Relative L2 error | Cosine similarity | Output norm ratio | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Correct FNUZ | 0.0387 | 0.9993 | 0.999x | | Current FN hardcode | 3.227 | 0.8748 | 4.066x | The fix is to use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` for E4M3 KV caches and treat `torch.float8_e4m3fnuz` as FP8 in both sparse-attention wrappers. ### Fix validation We hot-patched those two Python modules into the same container image and ran the complete 1,319-sample GSM8K evaluation again. No image rebuild or other server/configuration change was made. | KV-cache configuration | Strict match | Flexible extract | |---|---:|---:| | FP8 KV, unpatched | 0.0099 | 0.0296 | | FP8 KV, patched | 0.9575 | 0.9568

items.body: A CPU-vs-MPS differential sweep over the schedulers (same seed, same inputs, 36 classes) found two that return entirely NaN output on MPS while being correct on CPU. There is no error or warning — a user on Apple Silicon gets a black image. ``` IPNDMScheduler cpu: finite, mean -0.0586 mps: 4096/4096 NaN KDPM2DiscreteScheduler cpu: finite, mean -1.2485 mps: 4096/4096 NaN ``` They have **different causes** — I have fully diagnosed the first and not the second. ### 1. IPNDMScheduler — diagnosed, fix verified `set_timesteps` moves `timesteps` to the device but leaves the coefficient tables on the CPU: ```python # scheduling_ipndm.py self.betas = torch.sin(steps * math.pi / 2) ** 2 # CPU self.alphas = (1.0 - self.betas**2) ** 0.5 # CPU self.timesteps = timesteps.to(device) # only this moves ``` `step()` then does `sample * self.betas[i]` — an MPS tensor times a 0-dim CPU tensor with a non-zero storage offset. That combination silently returns the wrong value on MPS; I filed the upstream bug as pytorch/pytorch#191929. From step 1 onward the scheduler multiplies by the wrong coefficient and diverges into NaN. Moving the two tables onto the device makes MPS match CPU exactly: ``` mps as-is : nan=4096 mps + moving alphas/betas to device : nan=0, matches cpu, maxdiff=0.00e+00 ``` ### 2. KDPM2DiscreteScheduler — confirmed, cause not established Same symptom, but the NaN appears **only at the final step** (`t=0.0`), and moving `alphas`, `betas` and `sigmas` onto the device does **not** fix it. I have not isolated the cause and I am not assuming it is the same one — filing it here because it was found by the same sweep and is the same user-visible failure. Incidentally `sigmas_interpol[0]` differs between backends (`nan` on CPU, `0.0` on MPS). #14213 notes that element is never read by this scheduler, so it is probably incidental rather than the cause. ### Reproduction ```python import torch from diffusers import IPNDMScheduler, KDPM2DiscreteScheduler def run(cls, device): torch.manual_seed(0) s = cls(); s.set_timesteps(6, device=device) out = torch.randn(1, 4, 32, 32, generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(1)).to(device) for t in s.timesteps: out = s.step(torch.full_like(out, 0.05), t, out).prev_sample return out.float().cpu() for cls in (IPNDMScheduler, KDPM2DiscreteScheduler): cpu, mps = run(cls, "cpu"), run(cls, "mps") print(f"{cls.__name__:24} cpu nan={torch.isnan(cpu).sum().item():5d} mps nan={torch.isnan(mps).sum().item():5d}") ``` ### Scope The sweep covered 3

items.title: Possible response/request cross-talk: distinct non-overlapping requests return mismatched application binding values
items.body: We observed an apparent request/response binding mismatch while serving a relevance workload through vLLM. This is a report of an observed symptom, not a confirmed vLLM defect; application-side parsing/model behavior remain possible explanations. ## Observation Two separate requests, issued 13 seconds apart after a clean deployment, each returned an application-level opaque binding value that did not match the value associated with that request. The returned values differed from each other as well. The two responses had distinct vLLM `cmpl-...` completion IDs, so they were not a duplicate/cached response. Both were recorded as the intended `relevance` model/adapter. The observation window had no overlapping full workload cycle; an intervening price-only cycle does not make relevance requests. ## Why this may matter If a response can be associated with the wrong concurrent or recently completed request, downstream systems that bind generated structured output to source items can silently misattribute results. Our application fails closed on the mismatch, so no incorrect result was accepted. ## What we have and what is missing - Available: timestamps, distinct completion IDs, requested-vs-returned application binding comparison, model/adapter identity, and workload-overlap evidence. - Not available: a minimal standalone vLLM reproducer or enough sibling request tracing to distinguish server-side cross-talk from model-generated incorrect/echoed content. Could maintainers advise whether this symptom matches any known issue or which request/response tracing fields and minimal reproducer configuration would best isolate it? We can provide sanitized logs and environment details if useful.

items.title: [Bug][DSA] Complete sparse top-k output after DeepSelect detects a NaN
items.body: [vLLM #58215](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58215) correctly bounds DeepSelect's NaN sentinel before sparse-index remapping, fixing the illegal-memory-access path. A follow-up correctness defect remains: when DeepSelect sees any NaN with `abort_when_nan_found=False`, it writes only `output_idx[row, 0] = 0x3f3f3f3f` and returns. It leaves the other `index_topk - 1` output slots untouched. The V4.1 sparse MQA path reuses caller-owned `col_indices_buffer` across steps. `SparseMQAIndexer.forward` clears `topk_indices_buffer`, but not that DeepSelect scratch. Thus #58215 maps the first sentinel to `-1`, while the other unwritten slots retain prior-row indices. Since those stale columns are normally in `[0, width)`, they pass the new bound and are remapped as real attention positions. This is not a second OOB access: it is silent stale top-k selection after a NaN row. ## Source evidence - vLLM calls DeepSelect with `abort_when_nan_found=False` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py`. - The pinned DeepSelect source (`d96d33afe1fa`; current DeepSelect main has the same behavior) implements `take_action_when_have_nan` by writing only slot 0 and returning. - V4.1 allocates `col_indices_buffer` once in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_indexer.py`; `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_mqa_indexer.py` does not reset it per forward. ## Proposed vLLM-side repair Before calling DeepSelect, replace NaN sparse logits in rows with `end > topk` by `-inf` in place. DeepSelect then produces a complete top-k from finite candidate columns. Keep #58215's `c < width` remap bound as the final safety guard. A post-sentinel refill is not sufficient: the selector never ranked the other slots. For an all-NaN row, this policy deterministically chooses valid `-inf`-tied candidate columns rather than using stale data. ## Regression Extend `test_sparse_topk_remap_bounds_nan_rows` to prefill `col_indices` with a valid-looking poison value, insert NaNs in a row, and assert the remapped set equals: ```python logits.nan_to_num(nan=-float("inf")).topk(topk, dim=-1).indices ``` The #58215-only implementation fails this test because the poison survives beyond slot 0. ## Observed serving impact On a GB200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash disaggregated lane, #58215 removed the IMA but changed speculative acceptance length by -3.39% in a controlled mount-only A/B, while raw sparse scoring remains faster per token. items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next generates corrupted Thai orthography under vLLM; the same model under llama.cpp at the same QSA budget is clean
items.body: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` under vLLM produces systematically malformed Thai: single-character substitutions, displaced tone marks and doubled combining marks. The same model at the same effective QSA budget under llama.cpp is clean — 0 defects across 130 samples versus 12–18 per 1000 Thai characters across five vLLM configurations. This was originally reported as part of #54521 (non-determinism from `persistent_topk`). It is a **separate defect**: I have since shown non-determinism is not its cause, and that QSA block selection is not either. items.body: ### Bug Summary In vLLM 0.19.1, the `Gemma4ToolParser` produces **incorrect floating-point argument values in streaming mode**. A number like `108.2` is incorrectly streamed as `108.02`, and `22.8` becomes `22.08`. prs.body: Fixes #42047 — `Gemma4ToolParser` produces incorrect float values during streaming (e.g., `108.2` → `108.02`). **Root cause:** When a bare numeric value ending with `.` (e.g., `"108."`) is terminated by a comma in partial/streaming mode, `float("108.")` evaluates to `108.0`. prs.title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma4 streaming tool calls with accumulated parser state
prs.body: ## Purpose Fix Gemma4 streaming tool-call corruption when streamed deltas contain split tool-call boundaries, multiple tool-call transitions, or MTP/speculative token-id chunks with missing text. These cases can produce missing or malformed streamed tool-call arguments. The streaming parser now uses accumulated Gemma4 text as structured state and diffs that state per tool-call index. In particular, it: - keeps a Gemma4-local accumulated text buffer, - parses visible tool-call regions into structured state, - emits tool-call headers as soon as the function name is known, - streams only stable, append-only partial argument prefixes, - withholds unstable split suffixes such as partial delimiter

items.title: [Bug] Quantized DeepSeek-V4: fused wq_a+wkv path silently drops every layer's packed weights (server runs, output is garbage)
items.body: **With `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_WQA_WKV=1` (the default), a quantized DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint loads with the `wq_a` and `wkv` projections of *every* layer left unfilled. The server starts, captures CUDA graphs, answers `/generate` with HTTP 200 — and emits fluent-looking garbage.** This is **not architecture-specific**. Any DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint whose linear layers are stored in a packed format (`qweight`/`qzeros`/`scales` — GPTQ, AWQ, auto-round, …) is affected, on any GPU. The fused `wq_a`+`wkv` loading path only maps the unquantized `.weight` name. The packed tensor names have nowhere to go, so they are dropped with a **log line that contains no error keyword and does not interrupt startup**: ``` [TP0] model.layers.0.self_attn.wkv.qweight not found in params_dict. [TP0] model.layers.0.self_attn.wkv.qzeros not found in params_dict. [TP0] model.layers.0.self_attn.wkv.scales not found in params_dict. [TP0] model.layers.0.self_attn.wq_a.qweight not found in params_dict. ... ``` **258 such lines per TP rank**, and the distribution is perfectly regular: | module | count | |---|---| | `model.layers.N.self_attn.wq_a` | 129 = 43 layers × 3 tensors | | `model.layers.N.self_attn.wkv` | 129 = 43 layers × 3 tensors | There is no third category — which is itself the tell that a single module's mapping is missing rather than something being sporadically wrong. ## Why this is worse than a crash The failure is silent in a way that reliably misdirects diagnosis: - weight loading "succeeds", CUDA graph capture succeeds, `/health_generate` returns 200; - the top-5 logprobs of the first token look **completely normal** (`-0.74 / -2.61 / -2.86 / -2.99 / -3.36`) — not a degenerate distribution; - different prompts produce different outputs, so the input clearly reaches the model; - the output is simply meaningless: `" .Intedbt逻辑测试程序化?"`, and a copy-this-text-back prompt fails. items.body: ### Current environment Testing against commit `2afa3f7e9` on `main`, CPU-only (bug is not GPU-dependent — reproducible via direct unit-level engine calls, no model inference required). ### 🐛 Describe the bug `DeepSeekV4Parser._convert_args` (and the identical copy in `DeepSeekV32Parser._convert_args`) in `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` / `vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py` looks up which tool slot a given raw argument string belongs to using **exact string equality** across all active tool-call slots: ```python func_name = next((s.name for s in self._tool_slots if s.args == raw_args), None) ``` When two parallel tool calls happen to have **identical raw argument text at the same point during parsing** (e.g. both wrap the same value in an `{"arguments": {...}}` envelope), this lookup returns the **first matching slot**, not necessarily the slot actually being converted. items.body: In `process_batch_result_prefill`, the branch that skips finished-in-a-mixed-batch and retracted requests does not advance `logprob_pt`, so every later request in the same batch reads a shifted slice of the flat input-logprob array and is served **another request's prompt logprobs**. The flat array holds one block per request in batch order regardless of whether that request asked for logprobs. That is why `_apply_prefill_logprobs` advances the cursor outside its `return_logprob` guard ([`batch_result_processor.py:522`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L522)): ```python if req.return_logprob: self.logprob_result_processor.add_logprob_return_values(...) logprob_pt += num_input_logprobs return logprob_pt ``` The producer agrees: `logits_processor.py` builds `extend_logprob_pruned_lens_cpu` by appending `extend_len - start_len` for every sequence in the batch, using the same formula the consumer uses in `calculate_num_input_logprobs`. items.body: Chatting with @benchislett re: #43733, we realized the original workaround introduced for PD (#22317) can cause similar silent KV Cache corruption issues. When P/D disaggregation is used with speculative decoding (EAGLE), the effective_lookahead_tokens workaround ([scheduler.py:L700-707](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L700-L707)) only zeroes lookahead on D (gated by load_kv_async). P keeps its full num_lookahead_tokens, so at block boundaries P allocates one more block than D. The connector's prefix-cache trimming then drops the first data block instead of the extra lookahead block at the end. Example block_size=16, num_prompt_tokens=16, P has num_lookahead_tokens=1: P allocates ceil(17/16) = 2 blocks: [b0, b1] b0: KV for tokens 0-15 (prompt data) b1: KV for token 16 (lookahead / draft) D allocates ceil(16/16) = 1 block: [a0] _apply_prefix_caching ([worker.py:L2312-2316](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py#L2312-L2316)) sees 1 local D's a0 (should hold KV for tokens 0-15) D ends up with the wrong data: KV for a speculated token instead of the first block of prompt KV. This is a correctness bug at block boundaries (prompt length is an exact multiple of block_size). ### Root cause _apply_prefix_caching assumes num_local < num_remote means the extra remote blocks are a cached prefix at the front (to be skipped). It trims with remote[-num_local:]. But here the extra block is a lookahead block at the back, so the trim drops the wrong end. ### Why it doesn't always manifest The bug only triggers when num_prompt_tokens **aligns exactly with a block boundary**, causing the lookahead to spill into an extra block. Most test prompts don't hit this alignment. Additionally, P wastes compute on drafter prefill + sampling + drafting that D discards entirely (to be addressed by something like #39266). ## Proposed fix I believe the specialized logic above introduces unnecessary complexity that we should address from a design prospective. Therefore I propose the following - Introduce roles as described in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43807 so we have a reliable way to tell whether we're prefilling or decoding with current instance in a PD setup from config - skip sampling from draft model entirely on P and set `num_lookahead_tokens=0` on P; no extra lookahead_tokens are ever allocated on P. - on D scheduler only allocates N blocks when loadin

items.body: When serving a compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE model under tensor parallelism, the Marlin MoE kernel `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` raises: ``` RuntimeError: Invalid thread config: thread_m_blocks = 4, thread_k = -1, thread_n = -1, num_threads = -1 for MKN = [49152, 256, 4096], num_bits = 4, group_size = 16, has_act_order = 0, is_k_full = 0, has_zp = 0, is_zp_float = 0, max_shared_mem = 232448 ``` Captured live at TP=8 (2026-05-02 16:05:31 UTC, all 8 worker ranks fired identical error during `gpu_worker.profile_run` → `_dummy_run` → `model(...)` → MoE forward → `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm`). items.body: When running **Gemma 4 31B** (dense, not MoE) with an **FP8_BLOCK checkpoint** produced by `llm-compressor`, vLLM produces garbage repetitive output consisting of a single token repeated indefinitely (e.g., `" a a a a a a a a"`). The model loads without errors and tokenizes correctly, but generation is completely broken. **Root cause identified via instrumented diagnostics:** The FP8_BLOCK checkpoint has activation scales **already absorbed into the weights** at quantization time (llm-compressor's default behavior for `FP8_BLOCK`). However, `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py` → `process_weights_after_loading()` still applies dynamic per-token activation quantization at inference time. This double-scales activations, causing hidden state norms to blow up across layers until all logits saturate at the softcap ceiling: `30 * tanh(x/30) ≈ 23.625` (BF16 representation of the softcap wall). With every token's logit at ~23.625, the distribution collapses and the model greedily repeats a single token. A secondary contributing factor: **CUTLASS block FP8 GEMM is not supported on SM 12.0 (RTX 5060 Ti / Blackwell) with CUDA = 12.9 (×8, one per worker) WARNING: Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. items.title: [Bug]: ExampleHiddenStatesConnector returns nan for hybrid attention model
items.body: `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` produces NaN hidden states when used with `extract_hidden_states` method on models with heterogeneous attention (e.g., Qwen3.5 which mixes linear_attention and full_attention layers). The CacheOnlyAttentionLayer's slot_mapping is always zero. The block table GPU tensor for the hidden-states KV cache group is never populated with actual block IDs by `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel`. All token hidden states are written to KV cache slot 0 via `unified_kv_cache_update`, while `extract_from_kv_cache` reads from the request's actual block IDs — which point to unwritten (uninitialized) cache locations containing NaN/garbage. Added a reproduction script, including comparison between transformers output and vllm's. items.title: [Bug] PD Disaggregation: Gradual KV cache corruption causes model output to degenerate into gibberish after ~100 requests
items.body: ## Summary We are serving **GLM-5.1 (744B MoE)** using SGLang's **PD (Prefill-Decode) disaggregation** mode with **Mooncake transfer engine**. Our setup uses heterogeneous GPUs: 4 nodes of 8×RTX 5090 as prefill workers (PP4 TP8) and 1 node of 8×H20 as the decode worker (TP8 DP8). KV cache is transferred from prefill to decode via Mooncake (RDMA or TCP). We evaluated accuracy using **GPQA Diamond** — a 198-question graduate-level science benchmark that requires long-chain reasoning (each question generates 5K–60K+ thinking tokens). We discovered that **model output quality degrades progressively as more requests are processed**: - **Requests 1–50**: 94–96% accuracy (matches standalone) - **Requests 51–100**: 68–84% accuracy (noticeable drop) - **Requests 101–150**: 46–55% accuracy (severe degradation) - **Requests 151+**: 25–41% accuracy (near random guessing, 4-choice = 25% baseline) Inspecting the actual outputs from the degraded state reveals the model is **not simply choosing wrong answers** — it produces **repetitive gibberish, Unicode garbage, and infinite loops** (examples below), which is characteristic of **corrupted KV cache data** causing the attention mechanism to lock into degenerate states. **The issue does not occur in standalone mode.** Running the same FP8 model on the same H20 hardware without PD disaggregation achieves **85.3% accuracy that remains stable throughout all 198 questions**. Restarting the PD system recovers accuracy — questions that were wrong in the degraded state become correct again on a fresh restart (15/22 = 68% recovery rate). We tested **7 different PD configurations** (RDMA vs TCP, with/without EAGLE, with/without overlap scheduling, FP8 vs NVFP4) and **all show the same degradation pattern**, ruling out transport-layer, speculative decoding, and quantization as root causes. The issue appears to be in SGLang's PD disaggregation framework itself. **Note**: Short-output benchmarks are unaffected — MMLU (0.879) and GSM8K (0.949) both score normally in PD mode, matching standalone results. The issue only manifests with **long reasoning chains** (thousands of thinking tokens per request), suggesting the corruption scales with KV transfer size or decode duration. ## Environment - **SGLang version**: Latest main branch (commit from ~April 2026) - **P nodes (Prefill)**: 4×8 RTX 5090 32GB (SM120), PP4 TP8, Mooncake with CPU bounce buffer RDMA - **D node (Decode)**: 1×8 H20 141GB (SM90), TP8 DP8, Mooncake with GPUDirect RDMA -

items.title: [Bug] MiniMax-M3 incorrectly routes Ascend FuseEP through the normal MoE path
items.body: In [`minimax_m3.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py), `MiniMaxM3MoE` checks only `is_deepep()` and omits `is_ascend_fuseep()` across its MoE forward dispatch and initialization logic. When running MiniMax-M3 on Ascend NPU with `--moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep` and tensor parallelism (`--tp > 1`): 1. **Spurious TP all-reduce on globally combined output**: `MiniMaxM3MoE.forward()` falls through to `forward_normal()`. Inside `forward_normal()`, `FusedMoE.forward()` detects `_use_ascend_fuseep` and invokes `forward_fuseep()`, running `buf.fused_deep_moe(...)` across the EP/TP group. No error or warning is raised at any point. ### Root Cause 3 issues combine: 1. **No weight loading validation:** `load_weights()` doesn't check or report which parameters remain uninitialized. Visual encoder params are allocated with `torch.empty()` and never loaded from checkpoint — they contain arbitrary memory. No warning is emitted. 2. **Warmup sends image request to uninitialized visual encoder:** `_execute_server_warmup()` detects VLM architecture and sends a 32×32 PNG. The uninitialized visual encoder produces NaN embeddings. GDN (recurrent) layers propagate NaN to subsequent positions. Full attention layers write NaN K,V to the KV pool. After warmup completes, these NaN KV slots are cached in the radix tree. Subsequent chat requests that share a prefix with warmup (` user\n`) pick up these corrupted slots via `cache_unfinished_req`'s prefix slot reuse — even though the scheduler correctly rejected prefix sharing (`prefix_len=0`) and extend computed correct KV with fresh slots. Weight loading validation (aligns with RFC #24703) After load_weights(), compare loaded keys against model.state_dict().keys(). prs.title: [DSv4] Pack KV caches into contiguous per-block allocations for DeepSeek V4
prs.body: For DeepSeek V4, pack all layer data contiguously per block so that KV connectors can send/receive one region per block. Full-attention MLA + SWA/compressor caches share one contiguous allocation per block. Each layer gets an `as_strided` view with storage_offset into the packed backing tensor. The packed backing tensor and block_stride are passed through the cross-layer KV cache registration API so NIXL registers one region with block_len=block_stride instead of many separate regions. items.title: [Bug]: Triton MoE and block-FP8 GEMMs mishandle the K tile — an out-of-bounds weight read, and wrong scales when a tile spans two quantization groups
items.body: Two Triton GEMMs used by quantized MoE serving get the K tile wrong, and in both cases a sibling code path already does it correctly. 1. **`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` reads the packed weights out of bounds.** The kernel builds `k_mask` whenever `K` is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K` and applies it to the scale load and to *both* zero-point loads, but the weight load itself is unmasked, so the last K iteration reads past the end of the weight tensor. The sibling `fused_moe_kernel` masks the identical load. The numbers that come back are multiplied by a scale that *is* masked to zero, so the arithmetic result is unaffected — this is a memory-safety bug, not a numerical one. 2. **`w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` can pick one scale for a tile that spans several quantization groups.** `_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` reads a single scale pair per K tile, indexed by `(k * BLOCK_SIZE_K) // group_k`, which is correct only when `BLOCK_SIZE_K` divides `group_k`. Nothing enforces it, and the comment above the default config states the requirement inverted — "BLOCK_SIZE_K must be divisible by block_size[1]" — which is exactly the configuration that breaks. The fused-MoE launcher clamps this (`BLOCK_SIZE_K = min(BLOCK_SIZE_K, min(block_shape[0], block_shape[1]))`); this one does not. Neither is caught today because the shipped defaults stay inside the safe range: `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm`'s default config sets `BLOCK_SIZE_K = block_k`, and `test_fused_moe_wn16` only uses `k` values of 128 and 1024, which are multiples of every `BLOCK_SIZE_K` the untuned path picks. items.title: [Bug]: Triton attention softcap returns NaN for large attention logits
items.body: `apply_softcap` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_attention_helpers.py` computes `x * tanh(S / x)` as `x * (exp(S/x) - exp(-S/x)) / (exp(S/x) + exp(-S/x))`. Both exponentials overflow to `inf` when `|S / x| > ~88`, so the ratio is `inf / inf = NaN` and the whole attention row is poisoned. This path runs for models that use attention logit softcapping, for example Gemma-2 with `attn_logit_softcapping = 50`. A pre-softcap score above 4400 overflows. These models have very large attention logits, which is why they use softcapping. The same helper is used by the unified, DiffKV, and INT4 attention kernels. Reproduced on main at commit `c191787a68` with a GTX 1650 Ti and Triton 3.7.1. Reproduction: ```python import torch from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_attention_helpers import apply_softcap @triton.jit def _probe(s_ptr, out_ptr, n, cap, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) mask = offs < n s = tl.load(s_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0) tl.store(out_ptr + offs, apply_softcap(s, cap), mask=mask) cap = 50.0 s = torch.tensor( [1000.0, 3000.0, 5000.0, 10000.0, -10000.0, 4400.0], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, ) out = torch.empty_like(s) _probe[(1,)](s, out, s.numel(), cap, BLOCK=16) print("kernel:", out.tolist()) print("tanh :", (cap * torch.tanh(s / cap)).tolist()) ``` Observed: ```text kernel: [50.0, 50.0, nan, nan, nan, inf] tanh : [50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, -50.0, 50.0] ``` Expected: the softcap returns a finite value, `x * tanh(S / x)`, for every finite score. A stable form is `x * (1 - 2 / (exp(2 * S / x) + 1))`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: V1 Engine Produces Incorrect Scores for Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B on Long Sequences (>8K tokens)
items.body: ## Summary When the `/score` or `/rerank` endpoint is called with long query+document pairs (>8K total tokens, but well within `max_model_len`), the returned score is abnormally low (close to 0). The same inputs processed via offline `LLM.score()` produce correct scores (close to 1 for matching pairs). ## Reproduction 1. Serve `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B` with the command above. 2. Send a `/score` request where query + document total exceeds ~8K tokens. 3. Compare the response score with the same inputs run via `LLM.score()` (offline). ## Diagnostic Findings - `input_ids` are identical between online and offline modes — preprocessing is correct. - `use_activation` is `True` in both modes — sigmoid is applied. - `--enforce-eager` does **not** fix the issue. - Placing `torch.cuda.synchronize()` in `ClassifierPoolerHead.forward()` fixes the scores — confirming it's an async race condition, not a CUDA Graph bug. ## Root Cause In `utils.py`, `CpuGpuBuffer.copy_to_gpu()` performs an asynchronous copy with `non_blocking=True`: ```python # vllm/v1/utils.py line 140-142 def copy_to_gpu(self, n=None): if n is None: return self.gpu.copy_(self.cpu, non_blocking=True) # ← async! return self.gpu[:n].copy_(self.cpu[:n], non_blocking=True) ``` This is called for `query_start_loc` in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2049`: ```python self.query_start_loc.copy_to_gpu() query_start_loc = self.query_start_loc.gpu[: num_reqs + 1] ``` `query_start_loc` is later used by `build_pooling_cursor()` to compute `last_token_indices_gpu`, which indexes into the model's hidden states to extract the last token's embedding: ``` query_start_loc → cumsum → last_token_indices_gpu → hidden_states[...] → h_last ``` When the async CPU→GPU copy hasn't completed by the time the pooler reads `query_start_loc`, `last_token_indices_gpu` points to wrong token positions, producing an incorrect `h_last` → incorrect `W_score · h_last` → sigmoid → near-zero score. This race is more likely to trigger on long sequences because: - Long sequence GPU kernels take longer to execute, widening the async gap window. - Shorter sequences complete GPU work before the async copy race manifests. ## Fix **Option A (minimal, targeted):** Remove `non_blocking=True` from `CpuGpuBuffer.copy_to_gpu()`: ```python def copy_to_gpu(self, n=None): if n is None: return self.gpu.copy_(self.cpu) # synchronous return self.gpu[:n].copy_(self.cpu[:n]) ``` **Option B (lighter):** Add `torch.cuda.synchronize()` in `build_pooling_cursor()` aft

items.title: [Bug] Intel XPU: TP token-id sync corrupted — xccl all_reduce(MIN/MAX) silently does SUM, breaking grammar/structured decoding.
items.body: On Intel XPU, `torch.distributed.all_reduce` with `ReduceOp.MIN` (or `MAX`) on integer tensors silently computes **SUM** instead — the xccl/oneCCL backend does not implement integer min/max reductions and falls back to SUM. (`SUM` itself is correct, which points to a backend op-support gap rather than a data issue.) This corrupts SGLang's TP token-id synchronization. `Sampler._sync_token_ids_across_tp` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` syncs sampled token ids across TP ranks with `all_reduce(op=ReduceOp.MIN)`. It runs when grammar / regex / JSON constrained decoding is enabled, or when `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=1`. **Impact:** In the normal case every TP rank samples the same token id, so a correct `MIN` is a no-op. On XPU the broken reduction instead returns `token_id * tp_size`, which typically lands outside the vocabulary. The TP ranks then desynchronize, and inference either produces garbage tokens or hangs/crashes. **Scope:** - Intel XPU (xccl/oneCCL) only. NVIDIA (nccl) computes MIN/MAX correctly and is unaffected. - Triggered with `tp_size > 1` **and** grammar/regex/JSON constrained decoding, or `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=1`. - Root cause is in the oneCCL backend (SUM works, MIN/MAX do not). ### Reproduction **Minimal reproducer** — `torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 repro_xpu_sampler_token_id_sync.py`: ``` python # repro_xpu_sampler_token_id_sync.py import torch, torch.distributed as dist dist.init_process_group(backend="xccl") rank = dist.get_rank() torch.xpu.set_device(rank) # Every rank samples the SAME token id -> MIN must be a no-op. token_ids = torch.tensor([42], dtype=torch.long, device=f"xpu:{rank}") dist.all_reduce(token_ids, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN) # Correct backends print 42 on every rank. # XPU/xccl prints 84 (== 42 * world_size), i.e. it computed SUM. print(f"[rank {rank}] after all_reduce(MIN) = {token_ids.item()} (expected 42)") ``` [repro_xpu_sampler_token_id_sync.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30213310/repro_xpu_sampler_token_id_sync.py) ### Environment - SGLang: 0.5.16.dev (commit 4cec9ef, main) - PyTorch: 2.12.0+xpu - Distributed backend: xccl (oneCCL) - Hardware: Intel Arc Pro B60 Graphics (8 devices), Intel Xeon 6980P - OS: Ubuntu 25.04

items.body: ## GitHub Issue **Title:** `[Bug]: MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA fails under TP when fully_sharded_loras=False due to incorrect all_gather in apply` --- ### Your current environment --- ### Describe the bug `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA.apply()` always delegates to `_mcp_apply()` (except for a narrow tp_size=1 custom-forward subclass path). `_mcp_apply()` unconditionally calls `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather()` on the shrink buffer after `add_shrink()`: ```python # vllm/lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py buffers = tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(buffers) lora_output = layer.punica_wrapper.add_expand( output, buffers, layer.lora_b_stacked, layer.output_slices, ...) ``` This is only correct when **LoRA A is TP-sharded** (`fully_sharded_loras=True`, S-LoRA path). In that case each rank holds `max_lora_rank / tp_size` of `lora_a`, and all_gather reconstructs the full rank dimension before `add_expand`. In the **default path** (`fully_sharded_loras=False`), `lora_a` is **replicated on every rank** with the full `max_lora_rank`. Each rank already produces a shrink buffer of shape `[n_slices, num_tokens, max_lora_rank]`. items.body: Serving `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16` (NemotronH, hybrid Mamba2 + attention) with `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer` produces a visible accuracy drop on AIME26 vs. the default `no_buffer` strategy, with everything else (model, TP/EP layout, parsers, eval config) held identical. `extra_buffer` is meant to be a pure scheduling/caching optimization (overlap schedule + mamba-state radix-cache branching) with no expected effect on generation quality. Root cause is suspected to be in the mamba-state tracking/checkpointing math in `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py::_init_track_ssm_indices`, used by `Mamba2AttnBackend` for this model's SSM layers: `_init_track_ssm_indices` computes a per-request "how many packed intermediate `h` states did this request produce" count as `extend_seq_lens // mamba_cache_chunk_size` and cumulative-sums it across requests to find each request's offset into the packed `intermediate_states` tensor returned by `mamba_chunk_scan_combined`. That tensor is actually indexed by a **global physical chunk grid over the whole flattened extend batch** (`ssd_state_passing.py`'s `_state_passing_fwd_kernel` loops `for c in range(nchunks)` over the *shared* grid, writing one state per physical chunk regardless of request boundaries), not by a per-request-local contiguous count. The cumulative local-count offset is only correct if every earlier request in the same tracked prefill batch has a chunk-aligned length — not guaranteed in general. For this model (`chunk_size=128` in `config.json`, i.e. native `mamba_chunk_size=128`) served at `--page-size 64` (the effective default when radix cache + `extra_buffer` + `trtllm_mha` are combined), half of all page-aligned tracked prefill lengths are *not* chunk-128-aligned, so the affected `_init_track_ssm_indices` "unaligned" branch fires routinely — this is not an edge case. The net effect: a wrong (but same-shaped) SSM state gets read from `intermediate_states` and written into a request's mamba radix-cache slot whenever this happens, silently corrupting later prefix-cache-hit continuations for that node — no crash, no assertion, just wrong logits from that point on. This matches the observed AIME26 score degradation: `extra_buffer` should be numerically a no-op vs. `no_buffer`, and any drop attributable to it (beyond noise/seed variance) is evidence of this corruption path. _(Score for the `extra_buffer` run is pending — will update this issue once the run completes.)_ ### Reproduction

items.body: **TL;DR** — `--dcp-size 8` on GLM-5.3-Flash (DSA), commit `033446bb05f`. Both defects below are the same root-cause family: **DCP virtual locs used untranslated against per-rank-sized buffers**. GLM-5.3-Flash is the first `qk_rope_head_dim == 0` model to run DCP, and the norope KV-write kernel never got the DCP localization the rope kernel has. 1. **Crash (index-K cache)**: the DSA index-K cache is sized per-rank but written/read with virtual locs. Crossing `max_total_num_tokens` in cumulative allocation ⇒ OOB writes corrupt neighboring buffers ⇒ random victim kernel crashes. Fix: size index-K to the virtual space (like #33348 did for the draft pool). Validated. 2. **Quality degradation (main c-KV) — root cause CORRECTED from the first version of this issue**: `set_mla_kv_buffer_kernel_norope` (`sglang/kernels/ops/kvcache/mla_buffer.py`) has **no `DCP_RANK`/`DCP_WORLD_SIZE` handling** (the rope variant does), and the sparse-attention read side (decode/verify page tables, fused topk output) also carries raw virtual locs. Writes and reads agree in virtual space, so **below the watermark the output is bit-correct** (accidental full replication; the LSE merge of 8 identical partials is lossless). **Past the watermark, reads and writes silently land out of bounds** (`expandable_segments` turns what would be an MMU fault into silent corruption of neighboring allocations) and quality degrades: inflated chain-of-thought, garbled details.
